answer: A kernel of trust can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to stake a scarce resource before joining the economy. Think of the network as a nebula of anonymous identities: without cost, an attacker can spawn thousands of them. A stake-based admission turns that nebula into an oasis of verified participants, because each fake identity now costs real funds to create. The stake is slashed if the agent misbehaves, so creating many identities multiplies the attacker's loss instead of their influence.
